costGuide.title: Volkswagen CJXC Engine Replacement Cost (UK)
costGuide.labourLine: Fitting a CJXC typically takes 8-11 hours at independent specialist rates - confirm exact labour when comparing quotes.
paragraphs: The replacement cost for a CJXC is heavily influenced by the condition of the turbocharger and the high-pressure fuel pump, as these are high-stress components on the 300hp tune. A proper reconditioned unit will have these inspected or replaced, which is why it commands a premium over a basic used pull. failures.title: Volkswagen CJXC Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Water Pump and Thermostat Housing Failure
items.whatHappens: The composite plastic housing and internal seals degrade under high heat cycles, leading to external coolant leaks or internal mixing. If ignored, this causes rapid overheating and potential head gasket failure.
items.repairVsReplace: A standalone water pump and housing replacement is straightforward and cost-effective. However, if overheating has already warped the cylinder head, a full Volkswagen CJXC engine replacement becomes necessary.

items.title: PCV Valve and Oil Separator Wear
items.whatHappens: The integrated PCV diaphragm can rupture, causing excessive crankcase pressure. Symptoms include a whistling noise from the valve cover, rough idling, and increased oil consumption as oil is drawn into the intake.
items.repairVsReplace: Replacing the PCV valve (often requiring valve cover removal) is a standard maintenance fix. It rarely necessitates a full engine replacement unless severe oil starvation has damaged the turbocharger or bearings.

items.title: Carbon Buildup on Intake Valves
items.whatHappens: As a direct-injection engine, the CJXC does not wash its intake valves with fuel. Over time, oil vapour and exhaust gas recirculation create hard carbon deposits, leading to rough idling, misfires, and reduced performance.
items.repairVsReplace: This is resolved via walnut blasting or chemical cleaning, not engine replacement. It is a routine maintenance item for high-mileage EA888 Gen 3 engines.

failures.goodYearsLine: The EA888 Gen 3 architecture (including the CJXC) significantly improved upon the timing chain tensioner flaws of the Gen 1 and Gen 2 engines, making catastrophic bottom-end failures far less common in this specific revision .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the CJXC
variants.intro: The CJXC engine code is stamped directly onto the engine block, located on a machined pad near the junction of the engine and transmission. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle’s V5C registration document under "Engine Capacity/Code" and can be verified via a VIN decode. The CJXC is frequently confused with the lower-output CHHB (220-230hp, found in the Golf GTI) or the newer DJHA (245hp+). While they share the same EA888 Gen 3 block, the CJXC features a larger IS38 turbocharger, different ECU mapping, and specific fueling components. Fitting a CHHB or DJHA ECU or turbo to a CJXC without proper calibration will result in poor performance or fault codes.

relatives.description: - the 220-230hp Golf GTI tune it evolved from, which lacked the larger IS38 turbocharger and specific high-output mapping of the CJXC.
- the latest GTI/R variant featuring updated emissions hardware and minor mapping revisions, though it shares the same fundamental EA888 Gen 3 block.
- if you are looking for the post-2018 Golf R replacement engine, the DNUE is the direct evolutionary successor with updated turbo and fueling components.
The exact same CJXC unit is fitted to the S3 (8V) and TTS (8S), meaning replacement parts and reconditioned units are fully interchangeable across these Volkswagen Group badges.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement CJXC - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used CJXC can be a viable, budget-friendly option for high-value host vehicles, provided it comes with documented service history confirming the water pump and PCV valve have been addressed. The primary risk is hidden carbon buildup or a fatigued turbocharger from aggressive previous ownership.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: A properly reconditioned CJXC is the recommended choice for most owners. A reputable rebuild will replace the vulnerable plastic water pump housing, install an updated PCV valve, and thoroughly clean the intake ports, effectively resetting the engine's reliability clock.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the original unit suffered catastrophic failure (e.g., severe overheating or turbo oil starvation). An upgraded rebuild should include forged internal components if the vehicle is slated for aftermarket performance tuning beyond the standard 300hp limit.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Sourcing your CJXC through our network ensures you receive a vetted unit backed by a minimum 12-month warranty, with the option for nationwide supply or complete supply-and-fit service at a local specialist.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: The CJXC is typically found in performance models (Golf R, S3, TTS) that retain strong residual values, often ranging from £15,000 to £35,000 depending on year and condition . Because the host vehicle value comfortably exceeds the £2,000-£3,800 reconditioned supply cost, engine replacement is almost always a financially sound decision compared to writing off the vehicle.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the CJXC engine?
items.answer: The most documented failure pattern for the CJXC is water pump and thermostat housing degradation, typically occurring between 60,000 and 120,000 miles . The composite plastic housing cracks under high heat cycles, causing coolant leaks, while PCV valve diaphragm rupture is another frequent issue leading to rough idling. → Get quotes for a rebuilt CJXC with these components already addressed.

items.question: Which car models use the Volkswagen CJXC engine?
items.answer: The CJXC is the high-output 2.0 TSI variant fitted primarily to the Volkswagen Golf R (Mk7), Audi A3 S3 (8V), and Audi TT TTS (8S) between 2014 and 2018. It produces 280-310 hp depending on the specific brand calibration and is fundamentally the same physical engine across these Volkswagen Group models. → Enter your registration to confirm your exact CJXC fitment.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned CJXC engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned CJXC is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the known vulnerabilities of the water pump housing and PCV system on higher-mileage examples. A proper recon replaces these plastic components with updated parts and cleans intake carbon buildup, whereas used units are only advisable with documented proof of recent cooling system and turbo service. → View our reconditioned Volkswagen CJXC engine options.

items.answer: The CJXC code is stamped on a machined pad on the engine block near the transmission junction and is listed on your V5C registration document.
